memos.headline: AAPL Hits 52-Week High with Overbought RSI; CAT and GOOGL Trend Strong but Extended; PG Remains Weakest in Universe
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe: AAPL, GOOGL, UNH, and CAT are in powerful uptrends well above their 200-day means, while MSFT, JPM, and PG lag badly on relative strength. AAPL is printing a new 52-week high at 308.82 with RSI at 78.4—momentum is undeniable but the overbought reading and +14.1% premium to the 50-day mean make me cautious about chasing here; a pullback toward 270 (near the 50-day) would change my posture. CAT's 26-week return of +59% and +40.6% premium to the 200-day mean is the most extended name in the group, and while trend is clearly up, the risk of mean reversion is elevated—I'd need a break below 830 to turn outright negative. UNH shows the best 12-week relative strength at +27.3% vs SPY with RSI still at 67.8, making it the cleanest trend-following long in the set. PG is the weakest name: -15% from its 52-week high, -20% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks, and sitting below its 200-day mean—I see no reason to own it until it reclaims 150.

views.note: New 52-week high and strong trend but RSI 78.4 is overbought and +14% above 50-day mean argues for waiting for a pullback toward ~270.
Best 12-week relative strength in the universe at +27.3% vs SPY, RSI 67.8 not yet extreme, and only -3.2% from highs; would exit below 340.
Strong uptrend with +37.5% 26-week return, +29.3% above 200-day mean, and solid 4-week relative strength of +6.8% vs SPY; a close below 350 would change my view.
Massive +59% 26-week move and +40.6% above 200-day mean—trend is powerful but extension risk is real; would reassess on a break below 830.
Worst relative strength in the universe at -20% vs SPY over 12 weeks, below 200-day mean, and -15% from 52-week high; no reason to own until a reclaim of 150.
Still -22.8% from 52-week high and -9.1% below 200-day mean with negative 4-week and 12-week relative strength vs SPY; needs to reclaim 440 to turn constructive.
Healthy 12-week relative strength of +8.3% vs SPY but last week's -4.4% pullback and flat 4-week relative strength suggest momentum is fading near-term; watching 200 as support.
Flat 12-week return, -8.1% relative strength vs SPY, and hugging the 200-day mean—no trend to follow in either direction; would get interested above 320.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Post Extraordinary Earnings Growth; XOM and UNH Show Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I am struck by the divergence in earnings quality across this universe. NVDA's 2027Q1 filing shows $81.6B in revenue (+85.2% YoY) and a staggering 71.5% net margin producing $58.3B of net income (+210.6% YoY) on just $8.5B of total debt — this is the cleanest earnings power in the group. GOOGL delivered $109.9B in revenue (+21.8% YoY) with a 56.9% net margin and net income up 81.2% YoY, all on a modest $14.8B debt load, which signals durable operating leverage. On the other end, XOM's net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a 4.9% net margin, and UNH grew revenue only 2.0% with net income essentially flat (-0.2% YoY) at a thin 5.6% margin — both profiles suggest margin headwinds I am unwilling to pay through. CAT's 22.2% revenue growth and 27.2% net income growth at a 14.6% margin is encouraging, but $36.2B of total debt against $17.4B quarterly revenue warrants monitoring; a deceleration in orders would change my view there.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, 71.5% net margin, minimal debt of $8.5B — unmatched earnings power; would reassess if margins compress below 55%.
Net income +81% YoY to $62.6B on 56.9% margin with only $14.8B debt demonstrates durable operating leverage.
Revenue +18.3% YoY, 38.3% net margin, and net income +23.1% on manageable $40.3B debt reflect consistent compounding.
Net income surged 76.7% YoY to $30.3B and margin expanded to 16.7%, but $122.6B total debt keeps my confidence moderate.
Solid +16.6% revenue growth and 26.6% margin, but $82.7B debt load and slower earnings growth (+19.4%) versus peers temper enthusiasm.
Strong 22.2% revenue growth and 14.6% margin, but $36.2B debt relative to revenue scale makes durability uncertain.
Steady 10% revenue growth and 33.1% margin are respectable for a bank, but cyclical sensitivity limits conviction.
Defensive 18.5% margin and 7.4% revenue growth are fine but net income growth of only 4.3% offers limited upside.
Net income down 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin signals commodity-driven cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
Revenue growth of just 2.0% and flat net income (-0.2% YoY) at a 5.6% margin indicate stalling earnings power despite $77.9B debt.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% but Sticky 3.8% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue for Caution on Duration and Cyclicals
memos.body: I see a clear pause regime: the Fed has held the upper bound at 3.75% for three months after cutting 75bp over the prior year, while headline CPI is running at 3.8% YoY—well above target and suggesting the last mile of disinflation is stalling. The 10-year yield has jumped 48bp over three months to 4.56%, flattening the 10y-2y spread to just 49bp, which signals the market is repricing term premium and possibly fewer future cuts. Unemployment at 4.3% is stable but has crept up 10bp YoY, consistent with a mild slowdown rather than recession. In this environment I favor sectors that benefit from a positive curve slope and resilient nominal growth (banks, energy, staples) over long-duration growth equities that are hurt by rising real rates. A CPI print falling below 3.0% YoY or unemployment breaking above 4.6% would shift my call toward an easing regime and flip me more constructive on duration-sensitive tech.

views.note: Positive yield curve slope (49bp) and stable labor market support net interest income; banks outperform in a pause-with-positive-slope regime.
Sticky inflation and nominal GDP resilience historically support energy earnings; stable unemployment limits demand-side downside risk.
Staples pricing power in a 3.8% CPI environment plus defensive positioning as long-end rates rise makes PG attractive on a macro basis.
Rising 10y yields (+48bp in 3m) compress multiples on high-duration growth names; I stay away until the rate trajectory reverses.
Less rate-sensitive than pure growth peers given cash generation, but 4.56% 10y still a headwind for premium multiples; no strong macro edge either way.
Recurring revenue provides some insulation but rising long rates and sticky inflation limit multiple expansion; macro neutral.
Consumer spending resilience (low unemployment) offsets duration headwind from higher long rates; mixed macro signals keep me sidelined.
Cyclical bellwether faces cross-currents: stable employment supports capex but rising rates and flattening curve hint at slowing momentum ahead.
Ad revenue tied to nominal GDP which is supported by 3.8% inflation, but long-duration equity discount rate headwind keeps me neutral.
Defensive healthcare with pricing power in an inflationary pause regime; less rate-sensitive than tech and benefits from stable employment-based insurance enrollment.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: GOOGL and CAT Surged, MSFT and NVDA Sold Off — Divergence Creates Opportunities
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal available across the universe. GOOGL (+10.0%) and CAT (+9.9%) posted the strongest positive reactions on their Q-results 8-Ks, suggesting a genuine narrative upgrade that may still have legs given continued 8-K flow for GOOGL into late May. MSFT (-3.9%) and NVDA (-1.8%) drew negative reactions to their results filings, and MSFT's subsequent director-change 8-K on 5/14 adds a layer of uncertainty that could keep tone depressed. UNH's +7.0% earnings pop was notable but the follow-up Reg FD filing on 5/11 without a further catalyst leaves me less confident the positive momentum persists. JPM's muted -0.8% reaction and heavy governance-related 8-K activity (bylaws, material modification of rights, shareholder vote) suggest the market is digesting structural changes rather than a clear directional narrative.

views.note: A +10.0% earnings pop plus two follow-on 8-Ks in May signal a sustained positive narrative shift that may not yet be fully priced.
The +9.9% earnings-day move is the second-largest in the universe and suggests a sharp upward tone revision for an industrial name that rarely gets this kind of enthusiasm.
A -3.9% earnings reaction followed by a director departure 8-K on 5/14 points to deteriorating sentiment that may not have troughed yet.
The -1.8% post-earnings dip is modest and two prior director-change 8-Ks add noise; I lack conviction either way until tone clarifies.
A +7.0% earnings pop was strong but the subsequent Reg FD filing without further price catalyst tempers my conviction on continued upside.
Flat earnings reaction and heavy governance 8-K flow suggest the market is processing structural changes rather than a clear directional narrative.
A +3.2% earnings reaction is constructive and the prior director change 8-K appears benign; tone is modestly positive.
A -1.0% earnings reaction and a director departure shortly after suggest mildly negative sentiment drift in energy.

memos.headline: Oil at $100 and Rising Policy Uncertainty Signal Geopolitical Supply-Side Stress; Favor Energy, Caution on Tech Supply Chains
memos.body: I see a bifurcated geopolitical picture as of today. WTI crude has surged 50% over three months to $100.20/bbl, a move of this magnitude almost certainly reflecting supply disruption or sanctions-related tightening rather than pure demand—this is the dominant structural signal in the data. At the same time, the Economic Policy Uncertainty index sits at 227, up nearly 15% month-over-month even as it has fallen 45% from its 3-month-ago spike, suggesting that while the acute policy shock (likely tariff or export-control related) has partially normalized, a new wave of uncertainty is building. Credit markets (HY OAS at 2.78%) and VIX (16.76, down 14% m/m) are relatively sanguine, which tells me the market is pricing energy stress as contained—I am less sure. My key risk is that sustained $100+ oil feeds into input costs for industrials and consumer staples while benefiting integrated energy names, and that any escalation in export controls or China-related sanctions would disproportionately hit semiconductor and cloud capex names. A reversal in oil toward $80 or a visible de-escalation in sanctions policy would change my view on XOM and on the tech names respectively.

views.note: $100 WTI driven by what appears to be geopolitical supply tightening is a structural tailwind for integrated majors; multiple recent 8-Ks suggest active capital-market or operational disclosures consistent with a favorable environment.

Rising policy uncertainty (+15% m/m) likely reflects ongoing or escalating export-control risk on advanced semiconductors to China, which remains NVDA's key geopolitical vulnerability; no offsetting evidence of de-escalation.

CAT benefits from infrastructure spending but faces margin pressure from $100 oil raising input/fuel costs and elevated policy uncertainty clouding global capex decisions; two recent 8-Ks offer no clarity on direction.

Elevated policy uncertainty and the 50% oil surge suggest supply-chain and logistics cost headwinds for hardware-heavy names with concentrated China manufacturing exposure; no company-specific filings to offset concern.

Positive yield curve (10y-2y at +49bp) and tight credit spreads (HY OAS 2.78%) support bank earnings; geopolitical volatility can also boost trading revenue, and three recent 8-Ks suggest active engagement with investors.
Defensive staples name but $100 oil raises raw-material and transport costs; policy uncertainty is a modest headwind to pricing power in international markets.

plan.summary: Overweight GOOGL where fundamentals, technicals, and sentiment converge strongly; hold moderate positions in UNH, NVDA, JPM, and XOM where at least two analysts agree, while keeping ~30% cash to buffer rising-rate and geopolitical uncertainty.

plans.rationale: Strongest cross-analyst agreement: Technical (strong uptrend +37.5% 26w), Fundamentals (net income +81% YoY, 56.9% margin), and Sentiment (+10% earnings pop with follow-on 8-Ks). Macro analyst is neutral but ad revenue tied to nominal GDP is supportive at 3.8% CPI.

Extraordinary earnings power justifies a moderate position despite headwinds.
plans.changes_my_mind: Net margin compressing below 60% in next filing, or policy announcement of new China export restrictions on advanced GPUs.
